title: Deep vein thrombosis of the leg: diagnosis and treatment
subject: cardiology
summary: Use the Wells score to choose D-dimer or compression ultrasound, treat confirmed proximal DVT at home when appropriate with a DOAC (preferred over warfarin) for at least 3 months, stop after 3 to 6 months if provoked by a transient factor, and consider indefinite treatment if unprovoked or with persistent risk.

sections.title: Recognise and estimate probability
items: Unilateral leg swelling, pain, tenderness along the deep veins, pitting oedema or dilated superficial veins, especially after surgery, immobility, cancer, pregnancy or postpartum, oestrogens or previous VTE.

Wells DVT score (1 point each): active cancer; paralysis, paresis or recent leg cast; bedridden 3 days or more or major surgery within 12 weeks; localised tenderness along deep veins; entire leg swollen; calf swelling 3 cm or more versus the other leg; pitting oedema in the symptomatic leg; collateral non-varicose superficial veins; previous DVT. Subtract 2 if an alternative diagnosis is at least as likely.
DVT likely: Wells 2 or more. DVT unlikely: 1 or less.
Ask about PE symptoms (breathlessness, chest pain, syncope) in every patient with DVT.

sections.title: Diagnostic pathway
items: DVT unlikely: high-sensitivity D-dimer first; if negative, DVT is excluded. If positive, compression ultrasound.
DVT likely: compression ultrasound (proximal or whole-leg). If proximal ultrasound is negative, repeat in about 1 week or do a D-dimer; a negative D-dimer with negative ultrasound excludes DVT.
D-dimer is less useful in pregnancy, cancer, after surgery, in hospital inpatients and the elderly, where it is often raised.

Before treatment: CBC with platelets, creatinine (creatinine clearance for DOAC dosing), liver function, PT/INR and aPTT. Consider age-appropriate cancer screening for unprovoked DVT based on history and examination (not extensive CT screening).

sections.title: Initial anticoagulation
items: Start anticoagulation as soon as proximal DVT is confirmed; if suspicion is high and imaging will be delayed, start while waiting.
Prefer a DOAC over warfarin: apixaban or rivaroxaban can be started directly; dabigatran and edoxaban need at least 5 days of LMWH first.
Warfarin or acenocoumarol: overlap with LMWH for at least 5 days and until INR is 2.0 or more on 2 consecutive days; target INR 2.0 to 3.0.
Treat uncomplicated DVT at home rather than in hospital when there is no severe pain, bleeding risk, renal failure or social barrier.

Use anticoagulation alone rather than routine thrombolysis. Catheter-directed thrombolysis or thrombectomy only for limb-threatening DVT (phlegmasia cerulea dolens) or selected extensive iliofemoral DVT in specialist centres.
IVC filter only for acute proximal DVT when anticoagulation is absolutely contraindicated; remove it once anticoagulation can start.

sections.title: Duration of treatment
items: Primary treatment for everyone: at least 3 months (3 to 6 months).
Provoked by a major transient risk factor (surgery, trauma, immobilisation): stop after 3 to 6 months.
Unprovoked DVT or provoked by a chronic risk factor: indefinite (extended) anticoagulation is suggested if bleeding risk is acceptable; review yearly.
Extended phase after 6 months: standard or reduced-dose DOAC (apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily); anticoagulation is preferred over aspirin.

Isolated distal (calf) DVT with mild symptoms and no risk factors for extension: repeat ultrasound over 2 weeks is an alternative to anticoagulation; treat for 3 months if symptoms are severe or the clot extends.

sections.title: Special groups
items: Pregnancy: therapeutic LMWH by weight for the rest of pregnancy and at least 6 weeks postpartum (minimum 3 months in total); no DOACs or warfarin in pregnancy.
Cancer-associated DVT: apixaban, edoxaban or rivaroxaban, or LMWH, for at least 6 months and while cancer is active; prefer apixaban or LMWH in luminal gastrointestinal or genitourinary cancers.
Antiphospholipid syndrome (especially triple positive): warfarin INR 2.0 to 3.0, not DOACs.
CrCl below 30 mL/min: avoid dabigatran; UFH or dose-adjusted LMWH with warfarin, or apixaban with caution per label.
Recurrence on warfarin with therapeutic INR: check adherence and cancer; switch to LMWH.

sections.title: Escalate
items: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens (massive swelling, cyanosis, pain, threatened limb): urgent vascular or interventional referral.
Signs of PE, haemodynamic instability or active bleeding on anticoagulation: manage as emergencies.
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (platelet fall over 50%, typically 5 to 10 days after starting heparin, or new thrombosis): stop all heparin and use a non-heparin anticoagulant.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using D-dimer in a high-probability patient, or excluding DVT on a single negative proximal scan when probability is high.
Under-dosing the loading phase (apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily for 21 days).
Continuing anticoagulation indefinitely after a clearly provoked DVT, or stopping at 3 months after an unprovoked one without discussion.
Giving a DOAC with interacting drugs (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, some HIV protease inhibitors, azole antifungals).

drugs.name: Apixaban
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily; extended phase after 6 months 2.5 mg twice daily

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban
drugs.dose: 15 mg orally twice daily with food for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily with food; extended phase after 6 months 10 mg once daily

drugs.name: Dabigatran
drugs.dose: 150 mg orally twice daily after at least 5 days of parenteral anticoagulation

drugs.name: Edoxaban
drugs.dose: 60 mg orally once daily after at least 5 days of parenteral anticoagulation; 30 mg once daily if CrCl 15 to 50 mL/min, weight 60 kg or less, or strong P-gp inhibitor

drugs.name: Enoxaparin
drugs.dose: 1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours or 1.5 mg/kg once daily
drugs.notes: CrCl below 30 mL/min: 1 mg/kg once daily. Twice-daily dosing preferred in cancer, obesity or extensive clot.

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin (UFH)
drugs.dose: 80 IU/kg IV bolus, then 18 IU/kg/h, adjusted to aPTT 1.5 to 2.5 times control
drugs.notes: Severe renal impairment, possible thrombolysis or procedure, high bleeding risk needing rapid reversal.

drugs.name: Fondaparinux
drugs.dose: SC once daily: 5 mg if under 50 kg, 7.5 mg if 50 to 100 kg, 10 mg if over 100 kg
drugs.notes: Contraindicated if CrCl below 30 mL/min. Useful in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.dose: Start 5 mg orally daily (lower in elderly, low weight, liver disease), adjust to INR 2.0 to 3.0; overlap with LMWH for at least 5 days and until INR 2.0 or more on 2 consecutive days
drugs.notes: Many drug and food interactions; acenocoumarol is an alternative VKA used in India.
